newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil southeast rail section seen profitable.
newsitem.headline: Brazil southeast rail section seen profitable.

text.p: The MRS Logistica consortium, which has acquired a 30-year concession to operate the southeast section of the federal railway network, believes the section will be profitable, said the head of the consortium.

The consortium, which includes steel companies Companhia Siderurgica Nacional, Cosigua and Usiminas, mining firms MBR and Ferteco, fertilizer company Ultrafertil, transport groups Interferrea and Celato and the Bradesco Group, bought the concession for 888.9 million reais.
MRS has seven days to pay 30 percent of the sale price, with the rest paid in quarterly instalments during the rest of the concession period starting one year after the acquisition.

"This section is undisputably the best section of the federal railway network," said CSN's Armando Guerra, the head of the consortium. "We are convinced the railway will be profitable. No one would invest 900 million reais to transform the best stretch of the network into a loss making business."
The 1,674 km southeast section accounted for 40 percent of the federal railway's turnover and was the only stretch to post a regular annual profit.

Guerra said MRS planned to invest 350 million reais over the next four years to turn the southeast section, which links Brazil's industrial heartland of Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais, into a "state of the art railway".

Under the terms of the privatization model, the consortium would have to invest at least $227 million in the railway section over the first six years of the concession and $1.41 billion in the remaining period.
Guerra said the modernization of locomotives would be the first target. MRS plans to increase the number of locomotives in operation from the current 190 to 260.
He said the railway would be administered independently and headhunters had already been contracted to find executives for the job.

The controlling group of MRS Logistica, which is the new name of the railway section, is still being formed. The consortium will decide over the next seven days whether or not Bradesco and Interferrea will be included, Guerra said.
Of the railway's current 7,700 employees 6,600 will be taken on by MRS Logistica, he said.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
